subject: Extreme fitted values and issues including fixed priors

messages.author: e479c02cbfe48933
messages.subject: Extreme fitted values and issues including fixed priors
parts:
Hi, 

I am fitting inla models on datasets of different sampling strategies, including a factor of fixed habitat effects and spatial and temporal parameters, with a view to assessing prediction. I have 100 iterations of each strategy, and for some (i.e. iteration 27, below) there were no samples from one of the habitat classes and the resulting values are extreme in those areas.

e.g. summary(res$summary.fitted.values$mean)
     Min.           1st Qu.            Median           Mean                  3rd Qu.                Max.
0.000e+00     4.000e+00     5.000e+00     1.134e+71          6.000e+00         7.562e+72 

I tried to set some more restrictive priors to control this, but the priors don't appear to be affecting the model at all (the results are the same regardless of the priors I set). 

dat <- strategy1
it <- subset(dat, dat$iter == 27) # iteration 27 - problematic results, no built factor

fixed.priors <- list(mean.intercept = 0, prec.intercept=1/100, mean = list(hab=0), prec = list(hab=1/10))

# inla
coo <- cbind(it$xcoo, it$ycoo)
mesh <- inla.mesh.2d(loc=coo, max.edge = c(2, 4), cutoff = 1)
spde.a <- inla.spde2.matern(mesh = mesh, alpha=2, constr = T)
indexs <- inla.spde.make.index("s", spde.a$n.spde)
A <- inla.spde.make.A(mesh = mesh, loc = coo)
coop <- cbind(pred$xcoo, pred$ycoo)
Ap <- inla.spde.make.A(mesh = mesh, loc = coop)
stke <- inla.stack(tag="est", data=list(mos = it$mos),A = list(1, A), effects = list(data.frame(hab = it$hab, time=it$mon), s = indexs))
stkp <- inla.stack(tag = "pred", data = list(mos = NA),A = list(1, Ap), effects = list(data.frame( hab = pred$hab, time=pred$time), s = indexs)) # b0 = rep(1, nrow(sim_mos_pred)),
stkfull <- inla.stack(stke, stkp)
res <- inla(mos ~ hab + f(s, model = spde.a)  + f(time, model = "ar1"),
            family = "nbinomial", control.family = list(link = "log"), data = inla.stack.data(stkfull),
            control.predictor = list(compute = TRUE, link=1, A = inla.stack.A(stkfull)),
            control.compute = list(config=T, dic = TRUE, waic = TRUE),
            control.fixed=fixed.priors)

Can anyone advise or suggest why the fixed priors are not making any difference to the model output? Thanks!

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Extreme fitted values and issues including fixed priors
parts:
On Fri, 2023-07-07 at 01:33 -0700, Emilia Johnson wrote:
> f(time, model = "ar1"),

can you try with this one? sometimes, 'time' can take over


f(time, model = "ar1",
hyper = list(prec = list(prior="pc.prec",
param = c(0.5, 0.01)),
cor = list(prior = "pc.cor1",
param = c(0.8, 0.5))),
constr=TRUE)


make sure you have all time points, like 1,2,3,..., 10, in 'time'. if a
year is missing, like year 5, then add

f(..., values=seq(1,10))

f.example.



--
Håvard Rue
he...@r-inla.org
